candidate_relations.reason: Profound developmental delay is a feature of both benchmark syndromes but does not specify the concurrent MIC-CAP and Mowat-Wilson diagnosis.
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia could relate to epistaxis and vascular lesions but is a distinct etiology and omits the required composite diagnosis.
Ollier disease is characterized by enchondromas, which are not described, and is unrelated to the required MIC-CAP plus Mowat-Wilson composite.
Parkes Weber syndrome requires a characteristic fast-flow limb vascular and overgrowth phenotype, not reported here, and is not the benchmark composite.
Osler-Weber-Rendu is an alias for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia; despite epistaxis overlap, it is distinct from MIC-CAP plus Mowat-Wilson syndrome.
PHACE requires a large segmental hemangioma with characteristic associated anomalies and does not represent the required concurrent syndromes.
No defining connective-tissue fragility phenotype establishes Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and it does not match either benchmark component.
Gorlin syndrome has a different defining phenotype and is not equivalent to concurrent MIC-CAP and Mowat-Wilson syndrome.
MIC-CAP can be broadly categorized as a neurocutaneous disorder, but this label fails to identify MIC-CAP specifically and entirely omits concurrent Mowat-Wilson syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broad neurocutaneous family label lacking specific composite components
